title: Synchronization
body:
[[Critical Section]]
[[Concurrency]]
[[Producer Consumer]]

[[Locks]]
[[Bounded Buffer Problem]]

The spine of the course. Everything above is a piece of one question: **when several
[[Thread|threads]] touch the same data, how do you stop them corrupting it, without
serializing the whole program?**

## Why there is a problem at all

`count++` is not one operation. It is load, add, store, and a thread can be preempted
between any two of them:

```
Thread A: load count   (reads 5)
Thread B: load count   (reads 5)
Thread A: add 1, store (writes 6)
Thread B: add 1, store (writes 6)   // two increments, one happened
```

Nothing here is a bug in either thread. The bug only exists in the interleaving, which is
why these are miserable to reproduce and why you reason about them rather than test for
them. The stretch of code that must not be interleaved is the [[Critical Section]].

## The requirements

A correct solution needs all three, and dropping any one breaks it:

| Requirement | Says | Dropping it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [[Mutual Exclusion]] | at most one thread in the critical section | corruption, the problem you started with |
| [[Progress]] | only threads in the entry section decide who goes next | threads blocked by someone who is not even competing |
| [[Bounded Waiting]] | your time in the entry section has an upper bound | [[Starvation]] |

This is the [[Critical Section Problem]].

## The mechanisms, weakest to strongest

| Mechanism | Needs | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| [[Peterson's Solution]] | nothing but memory | busy-waits, two threads only, fragile instruction order |
| [[TAS]] | an atomic hardware instruction | still a [[Spin Lock]], still burns CPU |
| [[Locks]] / [[Mutex Lock]] | kernel support | blocks properly, but it is one bit: in or out |
| [[Semaphores]] | kernel support | counts, so it can express "how many slots left" |

Semaphores are the general answer because they *count*. A mutex can enforce mutual
exclusion but cannot tell a producer that the buffer is full, which is why
[[Producer Consumer]] needs three semaphores and not one lock.

## The cost

Every critical section is serial code, and serial code is the *S* in [[Amdahl's Law]]. Lock
more than you need to and you cap how much parallelism can ever buy you. The whole craft is
making critical sections as short as they can be while still being correct.
